answer: No. Your records show you did not have a blood clot in your lung. On the evening of 8 July 2025 you had a blood test (D-dimer) that was mildly raised at 0.92 (normal is under 0.49). A raised D-dimer can't tell clot from many other causes, so you had a CT scan of the chest with contrast to look for a clot. The scan report says: 'No pulmonary embolism. Lungs are clear. No pleural or pericardial effusion. Mild degenerative changes of the thoracic spine.' A 'pulmonary embolism' entry was made that day as a working diagnosis, but it is marked as refuted (ruled out) and closed. The diagnosis that stayed confirmed was chest wall pain, which was recorded as resolved by 22 July 2025. The 'pulmonary embolism' entry in your record is therefore not a real diagnosis, and it is worth asking your doctor to make sure it never gets read as one.
short: A July 2025 chest CT angiogram found no pulmonary embolism; the pulmonary embolism entry in her record is marked refuted, and the confirmed diagnosis was chest wall pain.
